name: Venet
lede: Venet is an old word for a Venice blue, a turquoise-leaning blue that dictionaries link to the Latin for Venetian.

sections.title: Venice blue, shortened
sections.body:
In Paterson's entry, venet is a turquoise blue, sometimes greyish, a shortening of Latin *venetus*, "of Venice" [1]. He adds that Maerz and Paul report the term in use in the fifteenth century for the sails of spy ships, camouflaged to avoid detection [1]. That is a single dictionary's secondhand account, and we treat it as a report and not a fact. Our library dates the name to 1425 from the same atlas [2].

The swatch here is a greenish teal; its nearest named color is [[sulphate-green]], with [[teal]] and [[turquoise]] close in feel [2]. It is greener than Paterson's blue [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color near Venet appears in 18 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.08 per cent, rarer than 73 per cent of named colors [3]. The earliest dated match is 1638, in a painting by Willem Ormea, in the 13 dated cases [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match shows a look-alike hue and not the Venetian color [3].
